newsitem.title: INDIA: India call ends steady, medium-term bonds in demand.
newsitem.headline: India call ends steady, medium-term bonds in demand.

text.p: Indian call money rates closed steady at 3.25-4.25 percent on Friday, against the day's opening of 3.75-4.50 percent, dealers said.
Some dealers said they expected the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to mop up 40-50 billion rupees at Monday's repo auction to arrest the call rates from dipping further.
At Wednesday's repo auction, the RBI mopped up 29.85 billion rupees, but call has been averaging below 4.0 percent.
"It is better for RBI to issue repos regularly as it yielded 5.00-5.25 percent against 8.10 percent on 91 day treasury bills," said a money market dealer.
In the securities market, the focus was seen shifting from the short-dated securities to the medium-term securities, a dealer at state-run bank said.
"The provident funds have picked up almost 10.0 billion rupees in government securities as well in corporate bond issues," he said.
The 13.65 percent 1999 stock rose by 11 basis points to 103.24 rupees, compared to its previous close, while the 13.40 percent 1999 stock rose by 15 basis points to 101.17 rupees.
